pairs.difference: A: the control desk is seen from high above. Its button deck and the riveted floor tiles tilt steeply toward the viewer, and the floor fills the lower half of the card, so it reads like looking down at a model on a table. B: the popcorn cart is seen from about chest height. The paving recedes gently and the cart's wheels and roof share that mild 3/4 view, which matches the real caravan and drum-kit cards.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera to about chest height so the desk's top face is only a thin strip. Turn the desk a little more into 3/4, and let the floor tiles show as a short, gently receding band under its base.

pairs.difference: A: the camera is low, near the dune line, but the dish is tipped toward the viewer so we see its bowl almost face-on. The dish and the cone body read as two slightly different views. B: the sandcastle is shot frontally at a mild height. Towers, bucket and beach all sit on one sand plane that recedes to the sea horizon.
pairs.fix: Keep one eye level. Show the dish turned in 3/4 like the cone below it, so its rim is an ellipse matching the ring at the top of the cone, with the cone base sinking into dunes that recede to a low horizon.

pairs.difference: A: the flip-flops are seen from above in 3/4. Both soles share one tilt and cast matching shadows on an implied surface. B: the planet floats with nothing to stand on. Its ring is drawn as a fairly open ellipse tilted one way, while the band on the sphere suggests a flatter view, so the ring and the ball don't quite share one camera.
pairs.fix: Tilt the ring so its ellipse runs parallel to the planet's stripe, as if both were seen from the same slightly-above angle, with the back of the ring hidden behind the sphere and the front passing over it.

pairs.difference: A: the taxi is in a lively 3/4 view. The road and lane stripes converge behind it and the car sits firmly on the road. B: the rover is shown almost side-on and flat. Its body box is nearly orthographic, the wheels face the picture plane, and the camera is high enough to show the whole top deck, while the grey ground is a vague blob with no readable angle.
pairs.fix: Turn the rover into a clear 3/4 view with the near front corner toward us, lower the camera so the top deck is only partly visible, and set it on a ground that recedes, with wheel contact shadows.

pairs.difference: A: the submarine is a 3/4 side view. The hull, porthole rims and periscope all foreshorten together. B: the rocket is tilted diagonally, but its body reads almost flat and frontal. The two fins point at different camera angles, one seen edge-on and one face-on, so it doesn't read as a solid object in space.
pairs.fix: Show the rocket in a gentle 3/4 turn: fins spaced evenly around the body, the near fin overlapping the hull, and portholes drawn as slightly squashed ovals that follow the curve of the body.

pairs.difference: A: the player is turned in 3/4 with a modest top face, and the earbud cables loop forward in depth. B: the saucer is seen from high above. Its top disc is a big flat even patch (planar share 0.64, the very top of the real range) and the rim lights wrap evenly, so it reads like a top-down diagram rather than a mild-angle hero.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera close to the saucer's rim level so the top disc is a thin ellipse, the dome rises above the horizon of the disc, and the underside of the rim is visible.

pairs.difference: A: the asteroid's craters face in different directions. The bottom crater is seen from below while the flame trail streams back and up, so the direction of travel and the camera angle don't agree. B: the neckerchief is frontal and symmetric, with a consistent slight top view into the collar loop.
pairs.fix: Pick one view: the rock flying toward the lower left in 3/4, with every crater foreshortened along the rock's surface and the flames trailing straight back behind it, narrowing with distance.

pairs.difference: A: the tiki bar is a tight, cropped scene from a mild high angle. Pool, stools and counter share one water plane, with foreground stools, the bar, and the hut behind as layers. B: the dome base sits small in the middle of a huge empty lunar ground seen from high up. The crater at top left is foreshortened more steeply than the craters near the base, so the ground plane bends, and there's no foreground layer.
pairs.fix: Move the camera lower and closer so the base fills most of the card, crop the ground into a short band under it, and draw all craters squashed to the same degree as the base's round platform.

pairs.difference: A: the telescope tube has strong forced perspective. The objective lens at top right is much bigger than the eyepiece end, while the tripod legs show almost no convergence, so the tube and stand use different lens strengths. B: the binoculars sit on planks seen from above. The barrels and plank lines recede together at one consistent angle.
pairs.fix: Use mild perspective on the whole telescope: the tube only slightly larger toward the lens, the tripod legs spreading evenly to feet that sit flat on the ground, all from one eye level.

pairs.difference: A: the bounce house floats on a sunburst with a mild high 3/4 view, and the arches and base share one tilt (planar share 0.002 only reflects its rounded inflatable forms). B: the water polo goal is a cropped high view onto the pool, and the goal frame, net and water plane converge consistently. Neither shows a camera inconsistency.

A: the shelf top is seen clearly from above as a wide sloping plane, but the helmet's round stand shows almost no top face, as if viewed at eye level. The visor faces us head-on, so hero and ground are drawn from two different heights. B: the sneakers sit on a floor that meets the wall at a clear horizon, and their soles and the floor share one gentle high view.
pairs.fix: Match the stand to the shelf: draw the stand's top as a visible ellipse seen from the same height as the shelf surface, and turn the helmet a little into 3/4 so the visor is an oval facing slightly sideways.

pairs.difference: A: the neon ice cream sign is flat and frontal on a wall, appropriate for a wall-mounted object and consistent. B: the lion is on a stepped pedestal in mild 3/4. The path recedes behind it and the trees are simpler background layers, all in one view. No viewpoint tell on either.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away through the camera. Often it sits too high: big flat top faces (saucer disc, control desk, rover deck) and a wide empty ground plane with the hero small in the middle. Or the hero is shown near-frontal and flat instead of in a confident 3/4 turn. The strongest tell is mismatched views within one card: a shelf seen from above while the stand on it is at eye level, craters foreshortened differently across one ground, fins or craters facing different cameras, or strong perspective on one part (telescope tube) and none on another. Real cards keep one mild eye level, crop the scene tighter, and stack the layers clearly: foreground, hero, then a simpler background.
